title: The Brake-Count
author: Dodd Carter, and another
body:
# Loads down

*Chalked on a slate under the bench, one line a load.*

---

Dodd, two loads, brake held. Ammet, one load, brake held. Dodd, two loads, a wheel off at the bottom, nobody hurt, the charcoal all over the road and Merrowhithe out with baskets before I was up.

*On the other side of the slate, in white, the same hand every line:* One stone. One stone. One stone. I am walking home. It is further than it was.

*Under it, in yellow:* Whoever you are, the Vale is south. You are going the wrong way round the Mere.

title: A Writ, Unserved
author: Hobb Tally, bailiff of the Charter
body:
# To Ansel Crake, debtor

*A writ of the Charter, the seal whole. On its back, in pencil:*

---

Thirty-one nights. He sits his side and I sit mine. He owes the Stilyard house forty marks and a boat. I am owed eleven marks in wages by the same house.

Tonight he asked me what the writ says. I said I could not tell him, it has to be served. He said then read it to the stone, and I did.

*Under it:* The stone did not pay either of us. We have agreed that it is the stone's fault.

title: The Clerk's Count
author: Pell Addock, clerk of the Counting Tower
body:
# Beasts seen at the trough

*A page from a Tallymen's day-book, the columns ruled in red.*

---

Kharrow, forty head. Tax owed, tax not paid. Bacon very good.

Rudd, twelve head and a bull. Tax owed, tax not paid. The bull looked at me.

*The last line, the ruling crooked:* No clan. Nine head, black, no mark on any of them. Drank the trough dry of salt and walked north up the gorge in the dark, and no drover with them.

*In the margin:* Not counted. I would not know what to write.

title: A Letter to the Guild, Unsent
author: Pell Addock, clerk of the Counting Tower
body:
# Sirs, respectfully

*A draft, much crossed out.*

---

Sirs. A pebble on the Forgiving Heap bears our mark and the sum of the North Road tax unpaid since the year 942, to the last penny.

I did not lay it. ~~I would like to know~~ I would be obliged to learn whether the Guild has forgiven the North Road its tax. If so, I would be obliged to learn what I am to count.

*Crossed through, and written again smaller:* If not, I would be obliged to learn who has.

title: The Trap Book
author: Nan Smoker of Merrowhithe
body:
# Traps lifted

*A line a lifting.*

---

Twelve traps, thirty eels, two pike that ate the eels, which we also count.

Twelve traps, nine eels, the beck low.

*The Toll's night:* Twelve traps, a hundred and four eels, every one white, the eyes like milk. They did not fight the withy. They lay in the bottom of the boat in a row with their heads to the north.

*Under it:* Berrit says smoke them. I say put them back. We have put them back. They are in the pool under the bridge, in a row, heads north.

title: Concerning the Fourth Stone
author: Gauder, miller at Brindle Mill
body:
# Concerning the fourth stone

*Nailed to a post by the stones.*

---

It is not me. I have three rights and I am glad of them. I do not need a fourth, and if I did I would ask for it with my mouth, like a clanless man.

It is not Gullhithe. They have rolled it into the Mere every morning for a month and they are tired.

*Under it, in a round hand:* It is the right to stay. Somebody wants the right to stay. Let them have it. J. W.

title: The Code
author: unsigned
body:
# The lamps

*On oilcloth, in grease pencil.*

---

One lamp: road clear. Two: the Watch on the road. A lamp lit and put out: come down, bring the boat.

No lamp at all: do not come.

*Scratched in with a pin, recently:* A green lamp: we are not the ones lighting it.

title: Hesper's Strake
author: Hesper Wick
body:
# What the Mere owes me

*Carved into the inside of a strake.*

---

One man, Tam Wick. One boat, this one. Four nets. A good knife.

Paid back: nothing.

*Lower down, newer and cut deeper:* I have turned my back on you thirty years. You have not come up the hill. That is the only thing you ever gave me.

*And under that, with a different blade:* She is owed a launching. The Wicks.

title: The Listener's Leaves
author: Ilse Varrow, Listener of the Circle
body:
# The rope, heard

*Loose leaves, the note written as a mark on a ruled line.*

---

The first year: the rope holds the fourth tine's note, a little flat, day and night, calm or storm.

The ninth year: the same. I have stopped writing it every day.

*This year, the hand quick:* The Toll's night: the rope rose a tone and has stayed there. The fourth tine is flat against it now. Something at the other end has got up.

*Under it:* Gone to the Spire. Touch nothing. Do not pull the rope.

title: The Watch Roll
author: the Gullhithe watch
body:
# Who sat, and what they saw

*Scored into hide, a line a night.*

---

Osk Wick. Nothing. Pell Gorry. Nothing. Osk Wick. Gulls, and a log that was a log.

*And so down the hide for forty years, nothing, nothing, the names changing, the nothings not.*

*The last lines, fresh:* Nobody sat. A stone came. Nobody sat. A stone came. Nobody sat. A stone came, and a wet track from the water to the cairn and back, and it was not a man's.

title: The Waiting Tally
author: the ward of Kharrow Gate
body:
# Sent down to wait

*Notched on a stick, and read out by the ward who cut it.*

---

A Tollmere man who said he did not hold with laws he had not voted. He said it back at dawn.

A Sayer who wanted to know what 'in kind' meant. She said it back at noon, having found out.

*The long gouge:* A woman in grey who said she had already said it, long ago, to a gate that is not there any more. She did not come up at dawn. She did not go back down either. She is not on the road.

title: A Smoker's Note
author: Wenna Smoker of Merrowhithe
body:
# To whoever takes the pike

*On birch bark, in charcoal.*

---

You are welcome to it. That is what it is for.

You are not to pay for it. That is also what it is for. A Kharrow token on Kindleday, a Rudd on Tallowday and an Oskel this morning, and Berrit says that is seven clans' worth of paying if we let you go on.

*Under it:* If you are more than one of you, come down to the smokehouses and we will feed you all. If you are one of you, and all seven, come down anyway.

title: Judgements Given at the Chair
author: as heard by Berrit Smoker
body:
# Last Tollday, at the Chair

*Written out by one who stood by.*

---

The net cut between two boats: each to mend the other's half.

The cow in the Wicks' reeds: the reeds to be the cow's until she comes out of her own accord.

The two brothers and the one boat: the boat to the brother who wanted it less.

*Under it:* Every judgement kept. Nobody has argued. We have never in my life not argued. Whoever it was sat very still and smelled of thorn blossom in the wrong month.

title: The Burner's Nights
author: Old Coll the burner
body:
# Nights at the clamp

*A stroke a night on a board.*

---

Ten strokes: the clamp done, opened, good black coal, Merrowhithe paid in fish.

Ten strokes: done, opened, good.

*This one, the strokes running off the board:* Forty. It breathes. I have not fed it since the tenth night and it breathes, in and out, the smoke going back into the turf on the in.

*Under it:* I will not open it. Whatever it is burning, it is not my oak any more.

title: A Trader's Reckoning
author: Jossel Ferrand, cloth-dealer of Tollmere
body:
# Kharrow Foot, the spring market

*A trader's reckoning, folded under a stone.*

---

Twelve bolts sold, the Oskel wife very hard to please and right to be. Four marks up on the day.

One bolt given against a blood-price for a quarrel I did not start, the ward says I did. Two marks down.

*At the foot:* Came down with my stone in my pocket, as a man should. Found it split in my pocket at the brow. Every trader's the same. The clans say it was not them. The clans have never in their lives said anything was not them.

title: The Bier Roll
author: Hael ko-Rudd, memory-keeper
body:
# Rested at the stone

*Notch for notch, as the Rudd remember them.*

---

Old Orra ko-Rudd, who counted the forty head. Rested, washed, sung.

The twins, born and gone the one night. Rested together, washed, sung.

*And so on, a clan's dead, one to a notch.*

*The last notch, and no name against it:* Cut in the night with a Rudd knife. Nobody in Ruddow dead. Every Rudd knife accounted for. I have looked for a clan's name to write here and my memory gives me one I do not have.

title: A Herder's Wall-Tally
author: the Rudd herders
body:
# Sheltered in the Wrist

*Scratched into the limestone, a line a night.*

---

Wind. Wind. Snow, and the dogs in with us. Wind.

Still. Heard the fingers.

*The last line, the stroke gouged:* Still. The fire leaned in and the smoke went up the throat of the hole like breath going down a man. The dogs lay flat. We came out and slept in the snow.

title: The Tinkers' Key
author: the tinkers of Oskel Edge
body:
# The marks

*Scratched on a tin lid.*

---

A pot: work here. A pot upside down: work here, no pay.

A chain: mend what they have, do not sell them new; they will not buy. A closed hand: they owe; say so at the door, softly.

A dog's head: walk past quickly, and do not eat.

*Under it, the newest line:* The mark with the eye and the eight strokes is none of ours. Nobody knows it. Old Mag says it is how you mark a hold before there is a hold there. We are leaving.

title: What Is in the Eye
author: Tobba ko-Oskel, aged nine
body:
# In the brakh's eye

*Counted by me on the way to the fold every day.*

---

A button. A button. A wool doll with no face, so he cannot look back. A bit of mirror. Two oatcakes.

The same. The same, and the oatcakes gone, which is the fox.

*Lower down:* There is a hollow in the offerings like where the dog lies. It is warm. The oatcakes are not gone. It is not the fox.

title: The Drip Book
author: Hild ko-Oskel, who keeps the Drip
body:
# Brought to the water

*A name for every child that drank.*

---

Brenn ko-Oskel, a boy, cried. Aila ko-Oskel, a girl, did not. Mother said she tasted it like a smith tastes iron.

*And so down the skin, generations of Oskel, the first taste of each.*

*The last line, the ink new:* Brought Dara down this morning. The water was warm and it sang. She laughed at it. I have not brought her back since.

title: The Answer
author: unsigned, in a Kharrow hand
body:
# The answer to the forgiving song

*Skerrish, on the back of a blood-price receipt.*

---

You forgive us every year
and every year we are still here to be forgiven.
We do not ask it. You do not stop.

We owe you a bridge. You owe us a silence.
Neither of us will pay first.

*Under it, in prose:* My grandmother taught me this and said never sing it. I sang it. It is a long walk down from the Hold and nobody stopped me.

title: The Stray Tally
author: the herders of Ghast and Oskel
body:
# Strays given back

*Soot for Ghast, scratch for Oskel.*

---

Three Oskel ewes to Oskel. Two Ghast lambs to Ghast. A dog nobody owned to whoever it followed, which was Ghast.

*And so on, twenty years of it, the soot and the scratch about even.*

*The last line, neither soot nor scratch, but pressed into the stone with a finger:* One grey ewe, no mark, given back to the cairn. Where she came from, she did not say.

title: The Watch's Inventory
author: the Dale Watch
body:
# Kept in the rock

*Burned into a board.*

---

One horn, ox, bound in bronze. Two jars of oil. Twelve torches. One sword, old, for whoever has nothing.

Checked every autumn. Oiled every autumn. Blown never.

*Under it, cut with a knife:* Blown. The night of the empty watch. The jars full, the sword here, the horn warm. Whoever called the dale called it with ours, and then put it back on its peg.

title: The First Drips
author: Kell ko-Brindle, tapper
body:
# Given to the stone

*Tree by tree, the first drip of the year.*

---

The Twisted One, gold. The Pair, gold and gold. Old Crooked, slow and gold, as he is.

*This spring:* The Twisted One, red. The Pair, red. Old Crooked, red and warm.

*Under it:* Every tree on the Rib road bleeds red now, not only the stand. I have not told the clan. I have given it to the stone anyway. You give what the tree gives.

title: The Oath on the Bench
author: cut into the stone; rubbed by an unnamed hand
body:
# The oath

*A rubbing, the Skerrish letters white on black.*

---

I swear by the bones I sit in that I will hold what I am given to hold.
I swear by the rope that I will not let go of the name.
I swear it to the clan that was before the seven,
whose verse is the one you do not sing.

*Under the rubbing, in ink:* Seven clans. Eight verses' worth of metre. Somebody has come to be sworn in. I did not take this to the Moot. I am afraid they would go up there and find the eighth seat warm.

title: The Keeper's Stack-Count
author: Varn ko-Skarl, keeper of the Moot Beacon
body:
# Peat for the beacon

*Knotted, and read out as knots.*

---

Thirty turves a day in the dry. Nothing in the wet. The stack as high as my chin by the solstice, which is enough for three sittings.

*Then:* The stack gone to ash in one night. The beacon cold. Me warm through, beside it, in the dew, as if somebody had sat by me and kept a fire for me in the only place I would not notice it.

*Under it:* The Moot is not sitting. Something is.

title: A Memory-Keeper's Warning
author: Hael ko-Rudd, memory-keeper
body:
# Do not say it

*On slate, propped against the stone.*

---

Four names have been cut off this stone in a thousand years, and not one of them is remembered, which is how it should be.

A fifth has been cut back onto the broken top. It is a living name. I have read it and I will not say it, and if you read it you will not say it either, because a name said on the Moot road is half an oath.

*Under it:* Whose oath? Who has he broken it to? Nobody alive has sworn him anything.

title: A Vigil Note
author: Rann ko-Kharrow, the night before
body:
# The night before

*Charcoal on sheepskin.*

---

The wolves came at the third hour and sat just outside the light and watched, the way my father said. I did not move. They did not either.

The fire is going. I have to let it. I do not want to.

*Under it, the charcoal fresher:* Somebody has lit it again. I let it go out and I sat in the dark and I heard someone come down from the bones and kneel and blow on the ash until it caught. They did not say anything. They sat where I sit, and the wolves lay down.

title: The Wood-Tally
author: unsigned
body:
# Carried to Dreughow

*Notched into the doorpost.*

---

A bundle a night. Ash and birch, split small, dry.

The price was forty head. Forty head is four hundred bundles, by the Moot's reckoning of a beast to wood. This is three hundred and six.

*Under it:* When it is four hundred I will knock. If they open the door, I will put the roof back.

title: The Fire Count
author: the children of Dreughow
body:
# Fires at the camp

*Chalked under the watcher's stone.*

---

Five. Five. Six (bar the door). Five. Four (somebody gone, Mam went down).

*And so on, down the stone, in many hands.*

*The last lines, one small hand:* The stone was turned round. I turned it back and counted. Five. Then I counted Dreughow, because the stone wanted me to. Eleven fires. There are ten houses.

title: A Word Sent Up
author: Brenn ko-Oskel, underground
body:
# To my mother

*Scratched on slate, sent up in the ore.*

---

I am well. The seam is good. The shaft sings the old verse at the change of shift and we sing it back, as we always do.

Someone has been singing it back a verse ahead of us. It is not a man on our shift.

Do not lay a pebble for me. *Under it, in another hand, the mother's:* I did not lay it.

title: The Ward's Log
author: Tosk ko-Brindle, cart-ward
body:
# Carts walked past the overhang

*Cut on a stave.*

---

Three carts, one taken, one Clanless hurt, two of ours. Two carts, both taken, ours not hurt, which is worse.

*Then, a run of the same:* Four carts. None taken. Five. None. Six. None.

*Under it:* They stand at the overhang and watch the carts go by and do not come down. One of them lifted a hand. I think he was a Brindle. I think he was my uncle.

title: The Carters' Oath
author: the ore-carters of Brindlecrag
body:
# The rhyme

*Cut on bark.*

---

Oil on the stone and the brake will hold,
The ore goes down and comes back gold.
Oil on the stone, and a word for the Three,
And the gorge will give the cart back to me.

*Under it, in another knife:* Somebody scraped it. Somebody left a link. A link off a chain is a man cast out. Somebody cast out wanted us to know he stood here, and scraped our luck off, and did not take it.

title: The Porters' Manifest
author: the Kharrow porters
body:
# Carried up

*Scratched on a board.*

---

Barley, six mules. Salt, two. A Sayer's books, one mule and the Sayer, who walked.

*The last entry, circled:* One crate, Tollmere seal, for Kharrow Hold. Weight of four mules. Will not split. We have not opened it. It hums when the Hold rings the hour and stops when the bell stops.

*Under it:* Sent word up. The Hold sent word down: we ordered nothing from Tollmere, and nothing from Tollmere hums.

title: The Link-Keeper's Roll
author: Ghalla ko-Kharrow, link-keeper
body:
# Links struck, links returned

*Scratched on an iron strap.*

---

Rudd, one link, for the forty head. Hanging.

Oskel, one link, for the shaft collapse and the men not dug for. Returned in 1031, when they dug.

Ghast, one link, for the bridge, the old matter. Hanging. Hanging. Hanging, forty years.

*The last line:* Ghast's link is gone from my line and is back in the bridge. The bridge stands straighter. Ghast has paid nothing. Kharrow has forgiven nothing. Somebody has decided on our behalf.

title: The Brother's Words
author: Dann, once ko-Rudd
body:
# Under the seat

*Cut into the stone, upside down.*

---

I can see the steam off the water where it falls past the stone. I cannot see the stone.

They carried it up for me. I was not allowed to thank them. I thank them here, every day, to the water.

*Lower, fainter:* When I am dead, let whoever sits here next be somebody's brother too. It is a good seat for it.

title: A Builder's Reckoning
author: unsigned
body:
# For the roof

*On a beam-end.*

---

Six beams, pine, from the Brindle Pines, cut on nobody's say. Forty slates to come. Turf.

The debt was a roof. The Brindle took my mother's roof in '19 and she died in the first snow. We took theirs back, all of us, and it did not warm anybody.

*Under it:* So I am putting one up. It will be nobody's. Anybody can sleep in it. That is the price.

title: The Gate-Warden's Count
author: Ossa ko-Kharrow, gate-warden
body:
# Stones at the cairn

*Knots on a cord, counted each first snow.*

---

My grandmother's count: four hundred and eleven. My mother's: three hundred and ninety. Mine, my first winter: three hundred and two. Nobody comes back over the Windgate. Some go.

*This winter:* Three hundred and two. Three hundred and three. Three hundred and nine. Three hundred and forty.

*Under it:* Nobody has gone over. Nobody has come back. The stones are dry underneath, as if they were carried a long way in a warm hand.

title: The Cutters' Tally
author: the ice-cutters of Kharrow Hold
body:
# Blocks down

*On a saw-blade.*

---

Forty blocks, clear. Thirty-two, clear. Fifty, clear, a good cold year.

*Last winter:* Forty-four blocks, clear when cut.

*Under it, the letters shaky:* In the cellar in high summer: forty-four blocks, not a drop off any. In each one, something. A hand. A bird. A cup. A face I know, which I will not say. Frostmother keeps what froze. She has started giving it back.

title: The Rope's Count
author: Maddra ko-Brindle, who says the names
body:
# Knots on the rope

*Said every morning, written down in case.*

---

Four hundred and eighty knots at the count of 1040. I say them all before the porridge. It takes the time it takes.

*This spring:* Four hundred and seventy-nine. One untied from the middle, the rope still kinked where it was.

*Under it:* I cannot remember what I said in that place. Nobody can. My granddaughter can. She says it is a girl's name, and she will not tell me it, because she says the girl asked her not to.

title: The Overseer's Check
author: Gann ko-Oskel, overseer
body:
# Up, and down

*Chalked on slate.*

---

First shift up: nine. Down: nine. Second shift up: eight. Down: eight.

*Last Kindleday:* First shift up: nine, down nine. Second shift up: eight, down eight. Third shift: none sent.

A third notch on the stone. Fresh. A third shift up the road that I did not send, that nobody saw go.

*Under it:* The mine sang till dawn, a full shift's singing. Nobody came down, because nobody went up. I have counted every Oskel twice.

title: Gann's Rope-Book
author: old Gann ko-Oskel
body:
# A rope for each

*Scratched inside the door.*

---

Brindle-face, the red rope. The twins, the two grey. The old nanny, the good hemp, she chews.

Tied every night. Checked at dawn.

*Under it:* Untied at dawn, every one, and coiled like a sailor coils. The beasts did not go. They stood and faced the mine as the old flock did before it went. Somebody is asking them. Somebody is also telling them to wait.

title: A Debtor's Tally-Cord
author: as read by the Rudd
body:
# The cord, read

*A knot for each thing owed.*

---

A death, Kharrow's, at the Rudd bridge in 1017. Forty head. A hearth. A name said wrong at a burial.

Too great to pay. Hung in the Hole in 1018.

*Tied into the end, in red thread:* Paid. And the knot the red is tied with is the paying knot, the old one, that nobody has tied since the Chain Years, and every Rudd who looks at it says it was tied right.

title: The Moot's Word on the Grass
author: the Clan-Moot, as copied
body:
# On the grass of Skarldale

*Written on a shoulder-blade.*

---

The grass is Skarl's, say the Skarl. The grass is Rudd's, say the Rudd. Sixty years; a keep burned; two sons.

The Moot says: the grass is nobody's. Let it grow. Let whoever is hungry graze it, and nobody be asked whose they are.

*Under it, fresh:* Both marks cut back, side by side. Not to say the grass is both clans'. To say both clans are the grass's.

title: The Smelt-Book
author: the Smeltings
body:
# Laid on the stone

*Burned into the board.*

---

Iron, the spring smelt. Laid, taken up at dawn, cold.

Silver, the night smelt, the pipes playing. Laid, taken up, cold.

*This month:* Silver, laid. At dawn, gone, and in its place a lead casting of a hand, a child's size, palm up, warm.

*Under it:* Palm up, like the Fallen Hand. We have not cast anything in that shape. We would not know how to make the fingers.

title: The Namers' List
author: the clan of Kharrow
body:
# Waited, and crossed

*Cut into the stool.*

---

Torra ko-Kharrow, crossed. Brask ko-Kharrow, crossed. Olla ko-Kharrow, fell, fished out at the Hold, named Olla Fished, and proud of it.

*The last name, cut deep in a sure hand:* A girl, no clan. Crossed at dawn, running, which nobody does. Asked at the Hold what she was to be called. We could not tell her. She said then she would keep the one she had, and did not tell us it.

title: The Chain-Ward's Chalk
author: Fedd ko-Ghast, chain-ward
body:
# News paid at the chain

*Copied off the stone.*

---

A Vale man: the cider's up a penny. A tinker: Oskel's buying chain. A Sayer: the Circle has an opinion. (She would not say what.)

*Yesterday, chalked in my hand and not by me:* The Moot will sit in the Rib Cathedral on the ninth day of next week, and eight will come, and there are seven seats.

*Under it:* I have not been to the Moot. I cannot chalk that well. I have told the Ghast and the Brindle both, and both think I am being funny.

title: The Smelters' Names
author: the smelters of Brindlecrag
body:
# First slag

*Painted on slag.*

---

Oskarth ko-Brindle, green. His father, black and bubbled. Ghalorn ko-Rudd, who married in, brown, and we let him.

*And so on, a lump for a smelter.*

*At the foot, newer:* One lump more than the smelters. Black, with a ring of silver grown out of it like a finger out of a glove. Whose? Nobody's first smelt. Somebody's last.

title: What the Stones Sang
author: Brenn ko-Oskel
body:
# Heard at the stones

*Notches on a bootlace, and what they mean.*

---

The shaft's song, the verse for the change of shift: true.

The shaft's song, the verse for going down: true.

*Then:* The stones, the shaft quiet: the verse for coming up. A verse behind. As if the shaft had sung it and the stones were late hearing, or as if the stones were singing it for somebody who has not come up yet.

title: How the Fire Is Laid
author: Tam Hollin, forester of Ormhold
body:
# The laid fire

*Cut into a slat of oak.*

---

Kindling of birch bark, dry. Sticks of hazel over it, three crossed. Oak split to a wrist, over those. Nothing green. Nothing taken standing.

Light it if you are cold. Lay it again before you go. That is all.

*Under it, in a later knife:* Somebody lays it better than this. Split wood so fine it rings, and a wood with a grain like pressed ash that I cannot name. I have walked the whole Wold looking for the tree. It is not here.

title: Rubbings from the Lodge
author: Ansa Pell, student of the Circle
body:
# The jamb, rubbed

*Charcoal rubbings, with notes in the margin.*

---

The chisel, the eye and the two strokes: the gang that cut the Stride's third mile. The same on forty stones at the Tollmere end.

The hand with the thumb out: the gang that cut the half block and stopped. Nothing else of theirs anywhere.

*Fresh, the rubbing sharper than the others:* The hand with the thumb out, cut this month, the chips still in the grass. The Circle says no Oroth has held a chisel in a thousand years. Then somebody has been taught.

title: What the Clansman Heard
author: Orrin ko-Skarl, drover
body:
# At the Leave Stone

*Scratched on hide.*

---

I asked leave, as my mother taught me, though the Wold never answers.

It answered. It said no, in Skerrish, the old way, the way my grandmother said it to her sons. It did not say no to me. It said no past me, over my shoulder, to something on the bridge behind.

*Under it:* There was nothing on the bridge. I went on into the Wold. I did not look back to see if the nothing went home.

title: The Torch Count
author: the woodfolk of the Northwold
body:
# Torches at the stone

*Knots in a pitch-stiff cord, read aloud.*

---

Three taken, three thrown, one given. Three taken, three thrown. Six given, a good week.

*This month:* Twelve gone in the night. None thrown. The gill lit at the bottom like a hearth with a ring of them, standing in the black water, not going out.

*Under it:* The weavers are not in the gill. The weavers are up here, on the road, where it is dark.

title: A Forester's Evening
author: Nessa Ashby of Ormhold
body:
# Fires on the fells

*Birch bark, a line an evening.*

---

Skarlow, four. The Black Keep, none, as ever. A drovers' fire on the Neither Grass, which somebody should mention to the Moot.

*The evening the bench was turned:* I sat facing the Wold, because it had been turned, and I thought I would see what it saw. I saw nothing. I heard the whole wood stop, the way a room stops when someone says a name. Then it began again.

*Under it:* I have turned it back. I would like whoever turned it to know I am not angry. I would like them to know I heard.

title: The Planters' Round
author: the planters of Elderhold
body:
# Notches answered

*Cut into a hazel stick.*

---

The Tally Hearth's sticks, this spring: forty-one notches. Forty-one trees heeled in: oak, ash, a rowan for the one that was a rowan.

*The morning after:* All forty-one planted, in a line, east. Nobody here did it. A line of trees going east to the Briar at a walking pace.

*Under it:* Elder says the Wold is sending the Briar what the Briar lacks. I asked what the Briar lacks. She said: the Wold.

title: The Tender's List
author: Wren Moss, tender at Mossgrave
body:
# On the bed

*Oak-gall ink on a board.*

---

Feather-moss, for old Sallow the bowyer. Taken; carried.

Cushion-moss, for the Larkfold boy. Taking slowly. He was small.

*The newest line:* A star-moss we did not start, already thick, and when I laid my hand on it I knew its name the way you know a word on the tip of your tongue, and it went. None of us can hold it. Somebody is to be buried who has not died.

title: The Vigil Roll
author: the Hart-Knights of the Wold
body:
# Vigils at the Mound

*Vellum, rolled in an antler tine.*

---

The watch of the dark months, kept by Ser Brannoc of the Tines. Kept. The watch kept by Ser Hild. Kept.

*This winter, in a younger hand:* Kept. And at midwinter I carried water to him, a cup, as the wood-people do. I do not know why. I did not decide to. My hands knew the way.

*Under it:* Something of him is in the water they bring. I think we have been keeping the wrong vigil.

title: The Brother's Strides
author: the children of Elderhold
body:
# How far he has walked

*Told to each child at the pegs.*

---

This peg is where he was when the Charter was written. This one is where he was when the Ash Winter came. This one is where my grandmother found him.

One stride a hundred years. He is going home. Home is the Moot.

*The three new pegs, one after another this spring:* He is not going to the Moot any more. He is going the other way. My grandmother says he has heard something behind him, and she will not say what.

title: A Count of Fires
author: unsigned
body:
# Fires to the east

*Chalked round the cold hearth.*

---

The verderer counts fewer fires every year. I count more.

One, on the Moot road, low, blue. Two, by the Hart Bones. Five, a line of them, walking north along the Briar on the Wold side.

*Under it:* They do not smoke. The trees they pass under do not scorch. I think they are not fires. I think they are what fire is for.

title: A Keeper's Mark-Stick
author: the keepers of Rookhold
body:
# At the root

*Notches on a stick, and what they mean.*

---

Visited: grey, dry, no change. Visited: grey. Visited: grey, a hound's hair on it.

*This spring:* Visited. Green. A shoot the length of a finger, soft, with the Briar's thorns on it no bigger than a cat's claws.

*Under it:* The wall is going grey and the root is going green. Either the Briar is dying at the top and coming back at the bottom, or it is leaving the wall and coming inside.

title: The Lamp-Runner's Card
author: Pip Tamwood, lamp-runner of the Hollow
body:
# Lit from the Hearth

*A knot burned for every dusk.*

---

I carry the coal in the clay pot from the Knot-Hearth to the Road Knot, and light it, and burn a knot here, and run home before the dark.

*The blue night:* I came with the coal and it was already lit. Blue. Not hot. My coal would not take from it and it would not take from my coal.

*Under it:* The Keeper says a fire not lit from the one before it is not one of ours. The Keeper asked me which way the flame was leaning. It leans away from the Hollow.

title: What Was Not Said
author: Hedda of Fernhold
body:
# The rest of it

*Bark-paper, folded small.*

---

You won, Corrin. You sat longer. The spring is yours, and the hunting under the Hart Bones is yours, and I will not speak of it again.

I will say it here. You did not sit longer because you were in the right. You sat longer because I stood up to go and help the child who had fallen at the pool, and you did not.

*Under it, in another hand:* I heard. The stones carry. I am sorry. The spring is yours. Corrin.

title: The Smith's Order Book
author: Hob Tines, antler-smith
body:
# Helms made

*The last pages.*

---

Ser Hild, a twelve-point, fitted. Ser Brannoc, a nine-point, the brow-tine cracked, bound in silver.

No apprentice. The knights say the Wold will send one. The Wold does not send apprentices, I tell them. The Wold sends weather.

*A new line, in soot, not ink:* One helm, six-point, small. For the one who comes after. Collect at dawn.

title: A Relic-Dealer's Prices
author: Mardle, dealer in antiquities, Lantern Row
body:
# Wanted, best prices

*Folded into eighths.*

---

Oroth antler (so-called), twelve points and over: eight marks. Under twelve: four marks. Any with carving: name your price.

Bring by the Stride's Foot road, not the causeway. The Watch has opinions.

*Under it, in a poacher's scrawl:* Eight marks. The Knights hung them back in the trees in the night and never touched us. I have been poaching eleven years. I am going home.

title: Wenna's Wish
author: Wenna Tamwood
body:
# How I would like it

*Tamwick paper, in a clay jar.*

---

A stone over me, with my name, so Tamwick can find me and say it.

A moss over the stone, with my name, so the Wold can tend it, and when the Wold forgets me let the moss go and let me go with it.

I would like both. I do not see why a person should have to be one kind of remembered.

*Under it, in a Woodfolk hand:* We have let the moss go. We did not forget you, Wenna. We let it go because you asked. Somebody else has not let go.

title: The Carriers' Tally
author: the oil-carriers of Fernhold
body:
# Jars to the Moot

*Notches on a yoke-peg.*

---

Four jars, the stones oiled, the hum steady. Four jars. Three, and the fourth spilled here, which is allowed.

*The morning after:* Four jars, empty, stoppers back in. The stones oiled, every one, better than we do it, into the carving. The hum a note higher.

*Under it:* Oiling is tending. Tending keeps the note. Something is tending the Moot that does not need to carry its oil.

title: The Verderer's Count
author: the Verderer of the High Wold
body:
# Harts counted

*On deerskin.*

---

In my grandfather's day: three hundred and ten. In my father's: two hundred and forty. The first autumn of mine: one hundred and ninety, the poachers busy.

*This year:* One hundred and seventy counted and notched. And then the notches filling with pitch, one a night.

*Under it:* I have counted the harts again. There are one hundred and seventy. None are gone. Something is not uncounting the harts. It is uncounting me.

title: A Carter's Question
author: Jossy Cooper of Tamwick
body:
# To the Hollow's children

*Chalked on slate.*

---

The loaf is for you, as always. It is the good rye, the one with seeds.

It has been here a week. The birds have not touched it either, which is not like birds.

*Under it:* If somebody has told you not to come to the road, tell them the carters are asking why. If it is one of us who has done something, tell us what. If it is not one of us, then I would like to know what it is, and I would like you to stay inside.

title: A Letter from Tamwick
author: the Larch family, formerly of the Greatwood
body:
# To the Wold

*In a tin under the hearth.*

---

We cut within bowshot. We knew. The oaks were straight and near and we were tired of carrying.

The wardens did not touch us. They stood all night and the lodge caught by itself before dawn. We have been in Tamwick eleven years and our children say 'Wold' the way Vale folk say it, as if it were a place.

*Under it:* We would like to come home. We will plant what we cut. We will plant it three times.

title: The Pickers' Weights
author: the foxfire-pickers of Hazelwick
body:
# Trays dried

*Scratched by the scales.*

---

Six trays, a pound and a half dry, sold in Tollmere for nine marks. Eight trays, two pounds.

*Then:* Went down on the ropes and the whole south wall was hands. Glowing, spread, palm to the rock, as if somebody had climbed the wall in the dark with foxfire on their hands and left prints the whole way up.

*Under it:* Up. Not down. Whatever climbed it came up out of the ravine.

title: The Rafters' Flood Roll
author: the rafters of the Wold Water
body:
# Floods, marked

*Oiled canvas.*

---

The year of the Charter: to the knee. The Ash Winter's thaw: to the chest, three rafts lost. The year of the Long Winter: to the chin.

The oldest mark: two heads over a man's head, no year, cut in a hand that is not a rafter's.

*The new mark, above the oldest:* Next spring. Cut deep and clean. We have taken the rafts off the Wold Water and hauled them up to Hazelwick. Nobody told us to. Nobody told us not to.

title: The Round-Book
author: the families of Hazelwick
body:
# Whose stool, whose year

*Between two hazel boards.*

---

Old Grandam, the Pells' stool, cut the first year. The Twins, the Hollins', the second year. Crookback, the Larchs', who are in Tamwick, cut for them by the Pells, who were paid.

*This spring:* Every stool cut last winter has come up with seven years of rods. Seven years, in one. The round is broken.

*Under it:* The Pells say it is their turn again. The Hollins say it is nobody's turn, the round is the Wold's now. The Larchs are coming home to cut Crookback.

title: The Locker Tally
author: the rafters of the Log Boom
body:
# In the locker

*Cut into the alder root.*

---

Poles: twelve. Ropes: nine coils. A boathook with a bent point, which nobody will throw away.

*This month:* Poles: twelve, wet every morning. Ropes: nine, knotted into lashings, the knots all rafter's knots, the lashings for a raft of twenty logs.

*Under it:* We have built the raft the ropes are for, to see. It is exactly the width of the Wold Water at its narrowest. It is the only raft that would go down the river whole. Somebody wants to go down the river whole.

title: The Watch Kept
author: Corrin of Fernhold
body:
# At the wall

*Burnt stick on bark.*

---

The grey patch by the fire: the size of a door. Countwatch says nineteen and the chalk running out.

Fell asleep at the third hour. I am ashamed of it.

*Dawn:* The fire out. The grey patch green, the thorns soft, as if the Briar had been fed. Ash in the grass, a line of it from the Breach to my hearth and back, the prints of bare feet, small, the steps of somebody who had come to warm themselves and found the fire was the wrong kind of warm, and had given it to the wall instead.

title: A Tamwick Toast
author: the carters of Tamwick
body:
# To the Wold, with thanks

*On the back of a press label.*

---

To the oaks that shade the road, the roots that hold it up, the Hollow at the end of it and the children who run down to meet us.

We do not ask. We know you do not like to be asked. We say thank you before, so it is said.

*Under it, fresher:* A fortnight full. The cup has a leaf floating in it, an oak leaf, green, in autumn. I do not know if that is the Wold saying no thank you, or the Wold saying drink it yourself, we are busy.

title: A Note Left in the Middle
author: Aldo, pit-man at the Sawpit
body:
# To my brother

*In big square capitals.*

---

ELEVEN YEARS. SHE MARRIED NEITHER OF US. SHE HAS BEEN DEAD SINCE THE WINTER.

I HAVE BEEN SITTING IN THE MIDDLE ALL WEEK. YOU HAVE NOT LOOKED. I AM SITTING IN THE MIDDLE UNTIL YOU LOOK.

*Under it, in smaller capitals, a different pencil:* I LOOKED. TOMORROW I WILL SIT IN THE MIDDLE TOO. THERE IS ROOM IF YOU MOVE UP. BRING THE GOOD CHEESE.
